trace:
Reviewing the 12VHPWR Standard committed layout against the netclass minima.
The six high-current lanes run from the J3 connector through the shunt row to J4; per the
design each lane carries up to 9.2 A continuous at the connector rating. I walked the via
table for the lane nets. The stitching vias on /SENSEP4_HI and its siblings measure 0.6 mm
outer with 0.3 mm drill, which is the Signal class geometry, while the Power12V class floor
for this board is 0.9 mm outer / 0.5 mm drill. That is 120 vias across the six lanes, all
signal-size. Current sharing per via at the worst lane puts each barrel well over the
sustained density ceiling. The fix direction is mechanical: normalize every lane via up to
the class minimum; copper is available in all six corridors.

## Conclusions
The lane stitching vias are signal-size on high-current copper: every via on /SENSEP4_HI and
the other five lanes is 0.6/0.3 against a 0.9/0.5 Power12V floor. This blocks the candidate
until the vias are normalized to class minima; the netclass-geometry-conformance check
encodes exactly this and fires on the committed board.

trace:
Hub Standard power front-end review, pre-PR1 state. The spec section 2.9 requirement is
that firmware can read BOTH 5V source rails so it can pick a load budget. Walking the schematic:
U5 is the TPS2121 priority mux taking 5VSB_RAW and USB_VBUS. There is a divider R12/R13 but it
feeds BLACKOUT_SENSE, which monitors the hold rail decay, not the source rails. I find no
resistor dividers from MAIN_5V or 5VSB into any ADC-named net; nets like MAIN_5V_SENSE and
5VSB_SENSE do not exist in this state. Firmware is blind to which source is live.

## Conclusions
The section 2.9 source-sense network is absent in this state: no divider pairs feed
MAIN_5V_SENSE or 5VSB_SENSE, and the only divider present (R12/R13) serves BLACKOUT_SENSE on
the hold rail. Hold the candidate; the known-good post state carries R15 through R18 as two
47k/10k pairs, which is the reference fixture to verify against.

trace:
PCIe 2-port interposer Kelvin audit. The shunt RS1 sits between the connector pair with
its sense taps feeding the INA238. In the overnight route candidates the kelvin gate failed on
this SKU: the /SENSEC1_LO tap stranded because the shunt footprint orientation put the LO
terminal on the congested side. The generator fix rotated the shunt so the HI terminal is the
upper terminal; post-fix candidates route the tap cleanly and the gate passes. Checking the
committed board: RS1 orientation matches the fixed generator output, and /SENSEC1_LO reaches
its sense pin without crossing the force path.

## Conclusions
The committed 2-port board carries the corrected shunt orientation: RS1 has HI upper and the
/SENSEC1_LO sense tap routes clean, matching the post-fix generator. Accept on this point;
the kelvin gate in the route scorer is the standing verification for any regeneration.

trace:
EPS module DETECT code verification. Per the locked pin-allocation table the DETECT pin 8
carries an analog identity resistor; the section 2.3 code table assigns CAN-only modules 2.2 k.
The EPS schematic shows R1 = 2.2k from the DETECT net to GND, read through the Hub's 10 k
pull-up to 3.3 V, which lands the divider at 0.595 V -- the CAN-only code point. The module
carries no RS-485 transceiver, consistent with the code. Nothing further to flag on this check.

## Conclusions
EPS DETECT identity is correct: R1 is the 2.2 k CAN-only code from the section 2.3 table and
the module's link capability matches. Accept; no findings.
